now been corrected reports indicate that a company wide go slow strike began at the end of june after the state owned port operator transnet port terminals failed to disburse an anticipated bonus payment to employees the strike has resulted in vessel berth waiting times of to days at the port of durban where of south african imports and exports are processed unspecified equipment failures are further complicating matters at the port however the most severe impacts are at ngqura container terminal near port elizabeth where total waiting times for berths have increased to days or more at at ngqura container terminal container loading has slowed from containers per hour to between and containers per hour this has had a significant impact on local agricultural cargo particularly citrus exporters who are in high season between the months of february and august citrus industry representatives additionally noted that the go slow strike has exacerbated pre existing challenges with low crane capacity limited cold storage capacity and limited container availability volkswagen one of the container terminal s largest customers utilizes the terminal as a critical transit point for parts supplied to their assembly plant in uitenhage the plant is missing its production target of units per day by approximately units losses are expected to intensify if critical parts for the just in time manufacturing process do not arrive soon a vessel with containers including some critical automotive parts is reportedly in the nelson mandela bay area but has not yet managed to berth at the terminal reports indicate that trucks have been forced to wait for up to hours for inbound and outbound shipments with members of local meat textile and electronics industries also reporting ground transportation disruptions expert testimony to media suggests that the cause of the strike was a critical failure in judgment by transnet managers historically transnet has announced incentive bonus payments on the morning that financial statements are released to the public such an announcement was anticipated at the end of june and it is understood that employees were under the impression that bonus payments would be processed at that time in a regular fashion however the financial statement release has been delayed by an ongoing audit that is not likely to be concluded until mid august and while labor unions representing transnet employees chose not to resort to industrial action non unionized workers expressed frustration at the handling of the matter and organized their own strike as evidence of their frustration this action was executed without sanctioning from south african courts which protects employees from being fired for strike participation at least employees have been suspended for their participation on july transnet announced that it has obtained an interdiction from the labor court of port elizabeth that orders striking employees to halt their action reports on over protesters detained at anti government demonstration in managua on saturday on saturday hundreds of supporters of the civic alliance opposition coalition gathered for a demonstration in downtown managua the action was intended to protest against the administration of incumbent president daniel ortega and to demand the release of political prisoners as ortega s government had previously outlawed anti government demonstrations security forces rapidly descended on the scene and forcibly dispersed the crowd with truncheons tear gas and rubber bullets nicaraguan authorities claimed that protesters were detained for violating public order the opposition claimed that demonstrators were detained and that six had been wounded by rubber bullets multiple news outlets and non governmental organizations have claimed that several journalists that were covering the demonstration were assaulted by police and or robbed of their cellphones there were no reports of injuries among law enforcement personnel assessment political leaders from the united states uruguay and multiple european countries condemned the actions taken by nicaraguan authorities on saturday representatives of the european union called on the ortega administration to respect the principles of freedom of peaceful assembly and freedom of the press nicaragua s opposition movement claims that people have been imprisoned on spurious politically motivated charges since civil unrest broke out across nicaragua last april the government freed detainees in late february and more were transferred to house arrest on march th nevertheless members of the civic alliance have deemed the concessions to be inadequate and the issue remains one of the major sticking points preventing the two sides from resuming negotiations as no solution to nicaragua s ongoing political crisis appears to be within sight similar bouts of anti government protest activity and ensuing clashes with security forces will likely continue to sporadically crop up in the coming weeks and months resilience continues to advise customers to avoid non essential travel to the country due to the risks posed by civil unrest and the government s arbitrary enforcement of laws

china allegedly stops buying all canadian canola seed exports in recent weeks beijing and ottawa have been locked in a contentious trade dispute over canadian canola seed exports to china on march china s general administration of customs gac issued a notice revoking the license of richardson international canada s largest canola distributor to export canola to china after it allegedly found dangerous pests in its products subsequently canadian reports on march indicated that chinese importers were allegedly unwilling to purchase canadian canola seed exports with industry experts suggesting that the restrictions are thought to be targeted at new canola sales rather than contracts already in place a second canadian canola producer viterra a unit of glencore plc also had its license revoked on march for an alleged similar pest infestation issue chinese customs authorities announced on march that leptosphaeria maculans and other pest infections were detected in richardson international s canola seed imports on multiple occasions at ports in dalian nanning shenzhen and guangzhou on march chinese media reports announced that further pest infestations including of the leptosphaeria maculans bacteria had allegedly been found in viterra s canola shipments at the ports of dalian and nanning diplomatic spats the unexpected ban on canadian canola products comes on the back of a diplomatic dispute that has been linked to the detention of a senior chinese corporate executive in vancouver last year although chinese officials and media sources cite agricultural safety concerns as the main reason behind the richardson and viterra decisions other reports suggest that diplomatic tensions between beijing and ottawa are the more likely root cause behind the seemingly retaliatory measures canadian officials have strongly refuted chinese allegations richardson has likewise rejected these claims while viterra has yet to comment in addition the canadian food inspection agency cfia officials on march denied canadian media reports that strict customs inspections were also being applied to other canadian agricultural exports such as wheat peas and flax seed some observers including former canadian ambassadors to china are urging the government to file an official complaint at the world trade organization but the canadian trade minister is calling on china to provide sufficient scientific evidence before taking any further measures it remains unclear as to whether there will be an outright ban of canadian canola imports or if another producer will follow richardson and glencore in having their import licenses revoked on april canada s agriculture ministry denied media reports that a third canola exporter was being targeted by china clarifying that there has not been another company to have their registration suspended regulatory ambiguity produces uncertainty canola a variant of rapeseed is used for cooking oil and animal feed for livestock but also as a source of renewable energy through biodiesel in some markets such as europe as the world s largest canola exporter canada supplies about percent of china s canola exports with million metric tons of canola seeds last year a volume that surpasses both the second and third largest exporters combined with the planting season looming in mid to late april the dispute comes at a crucial moment when canola farmers worldwide will need to decide on which crops to grow including wheat barley and canola given that many farmers have already finalized their investment and planting decisions the continued disruption is leaving canola producers and suppliers seeking canola exports with further uncertainty in the face of declining crop prices and regulatory ambiguity in china as of this writing beijing has not issued any official statements on whether all imports of canadian canola seeds are banned customers focusing on chinese industries will need to remain alert on any further potential regulatory disruptions on canadian agricultural products by customs authorities the ongoing canola dispute comes on the heels of another similar delay in customs clearance of australian coal imports last month understood to be as a result of diplomatic tensions between canberra and beijing

cocaine seizures at brazil ports rose by percent in risk of disruption for affected cargo brazil s department of federal revenue rfb recently announced that the number of cocaine seizures at ports in brazil has jumped percent between january and october of this year compared to the year prior authorities this year have seized tons of cocaine at ports compared to tons last year the majority of seizures have occurred in the ports of santos paranagua natal and itajai authorities found that traffickers would bribe port workers to break open sealed containers and hide cocaine inside while the companies shipping their legal goods would not necessarily be aware their shipments had been compromised brazilian authorities cited an increase in cocaine production in andean countries as a factor in the rise of confiscations while also remarking that training of rfb agents has increased and the majority of ports are now equipped with x ray machines assessment the apparent increase in cocaine smuggling through brazilian ports to destinations in europe poses challenges to businesses that could face shipment disruptions as a result of increased screening at ports or even delays or confiscations of legitimate shipments used by traffickers to conceal drug shipments chemicals and coffee have been among the cargoes targeted for smuggling although the netherlands france and belgium have been primary intended european ports of arrival for confiscated drug shipments through brazilian ports the rfb has recorded increased seizures of drugs heading to portugal and italy as traffickers attempt alternate routes with the aim of avoiding the scrutiny along more established routes for drug shipments while no major disruptions to port operations had been indicated by authorities in conjunction with the increase in cocaine seizures this year it is advised to be aware of the potential for delay or disruption from any major anti drug operations as well as overall efforts to improve screening at ports with high recorded drug trafficking attempts

arabian port of jeddah early on monday december according to saudi sources the british owned singapore flagged tanker bw rhine was reportedly targeted by a bomb laden boat at approximately am local time causing an explosion and a fire although the ship s crew and firefighters reportedly extinguished the fire the attack caused damage to the tanker s body though there are no concerns as of this writing of an oil spill reports also indicated that the attack shut down jeddah port though as of now it remains unclear if operations have resumed the bw rhine had docked at jeddah on december carrying over tons of gasoline from an aramco refinery at yanbu for consumption in the kingdom following the attack the united kingdom marine trade operations issued an advisory stating that an investigation has been opened and urging all ships in the area to exercise caution the attack has not yet been claimed by any group assessment the incident underscores the vulnerability of saudi arabia s oil infrastructure and highlights risks posed to commercial shipping in the red sea the explosion also marks the fourth such assault targeting saudi energy infrastructure in a month most recently a mine exploded off the coast of shuqaiq and damaged a maltese flagged oil tanker on november in an attack claimed by houthi rebels although saudi officials have not blamed anyone for the most recent attack on december bomb laden boats and limpet mines have been used periodically by houthi rebels in the past suggesting the shia militia was likely responsible saudis typically claim to intercept and destroy unmanned bomb laden boats however any damage to commercial vessels in this region has the potential to damage production facilities possibly affecting supply chains and oil prices as the red sea is a vital shipping lane for international energy supplies and other cargo if attacks successfully damage oil production or result in casualties this would further increase the risk of conflict in the area heightened security is likely at all commercial ports in the bab al mandeb strat in the red sea as well as the persian gulf in the coming days

chinese and hong kong business sectors targeted in string of measures in ongoing tensions with us a number of recent steps taken by the united states government have the potential to impact businesses with operational ties to china or hong kong as relations between china and the us continue to deteriorate this week the us commerce department further restricted chinese technology company huawei from using us technology by adding additional companies linked to huawei to the department s entity list the move is designed to stop huawei s access to us computer chips and other technology even generic products not expressly designed for use by huawei by requiring companies to receive authorization from the us before being able to sell technology to huawei or linked companies a full list of impacted companies is available here as part of the us s recent revocation of hong kong s special status under which it was treated separately from mainland china beginning on september products manufactured in hong kong must be labeled as made in china on thursday hong kong officials announced that they would challenge this change at the world trade organization wto on wednesday the us suspended multiple treaties that had been in place with hong kong including an agreement on reciprocal income tax exemptions for ships operating internationally and an extradition agreement with france and germany being some of the other most recent countries to have ended extradition to hong kong on tuesday the us state department wrote to american universities asking them to consider removing investments in chinese companies from their endowments and warning of the potential for chinese companies to be delisted from american stock exchanges the request apparently relates to a recent recommendation from a us treasury department working group that chinese companies be delisted from us exchanges if they fail to comply with transparency and accounting oversight regulations by january finally on monday us president donald trump stated his intention to formulate tax credits for us companies that remove manufacturing from china and warned that companies that keep operations in china may be blocked from receiving us government contracts assessment taken together the recent measures have the potential for strong impacts to business ties and could potentially draw chinese retaliation although china is probably more limited in its options to respond than the us huawei is one of the largest telecommunications and technology companies in the world the previous us restrictions placed on the company s technology access which were expanded this week had already done damage to huawei s operations according to company executives huawei had already been forced to make certain changes in response including by reworking supply chains according to us officials the additional restrictions are being enacted due to huawei attempting to evade the earlier regulations the chinese government has condemned the more recent moves against huawei but has so far not taken any direct retaliatory steps probably fearing that taking moves against american companies operating in china would be more damaging to the chinese economy in the past beijing has threatened to create a list of foreign businesses that it says represent threats to chinese security and take corresponding measures against them but has not yet officially done so the made in china labeling that will be required on hong kong products beginning on september is unlikely to have a drastic effect on exports from the city although it will put such products under the same tariff regime that applies to items from mainland china hong kong is more important as a reshipping point for logistics purposes and only around one percent of products that are exported from the city are actually manufactured there if the government does take the issue to the wto the initial call will be for consultations with the us there and will move to a dispute panel only if the issue is not resolved it is advised to remain abreast of developments as us chinese relations remain soured and to be aware of the potential for some form of chinese economic retaliation even if on a smaller scale in response to the us moves

and damages the storm also known as a derecho caused winds of almost miles per hour equivalent to a category hurricane cedar rapids the second biggest iowa city by population was one of the hardest hit areas in the central and eastern portions of the state eyewitness accounts in cedar rapids have described significant destruction with the majority of structures suffering damage and numerous local roads deemed impassable an estimated homes were damaged in the derecho across the state of iowa at least four deaths three in iowa and one in indiana have been blamed on the storm which also caused widespread damage across the rest of the midwest after moving east through iowa upwards of two million people across the region lost power including at least in iowa in response to the storm president donald trump approved a federal disaster declaration for iowa that allowed for federal disaster aid for the state in addition governor kim reynolds issued a disaster proclamation for were torn down and several thousand utility poles were damaged beyond repair linn county has also reported extensive telecom and internet outages in addition to the power outages the storm has also caused widespread destruction to iowa farmland with an estimated several billion dollars in damages initial estimates from the u s department of agricultural usda suggest at least million acres of any of the damaged crops are salvageable while the damaged crops are a major part of the iowa economy it is not expected that crop loss significantly impacts the price and availability of those products for u s consumers derechos most often occur during the months of june july and august and typically impact the central and eastern regions of the united states however they are much rarer compared to regular or severe thunderstorms to be classified as a derecho a storm much produces winds of at least miles per hour over a path at least miles long and has no more than three hours separating individual wind reports these types of storms move extremely quickly often between to miles per hour allowing them to cause damage over extensive portions of land the storms often form with little to no warning and the iowa derecho left residents with as little as to minutes to prepare for the storm this was the second derecho of after the first traveled through ohio pennsylvania new jersey and west virginia at the beginning of june that derecho also caused widespread damage killing four people and leaving upwards of a million people without power due to the widescale damage these vietnam bans scrap import to keep its ports congestion free since may major ports in vietnam such as cat lai port and hai phong port have faced severe congestions due to high volume imports of containers filled with paper plastic and metal scrap materials the congestion in vietnamese ports may partially be the result of china s ban on scrap imports since early prior to which it used to allow half of the world s plastic waste into the country due to the new environment policies adopted by china many waste export businesses were left to find new emerging markets such as southeast asia to import their scrap materials one country in particular is vietnam where waste import had increased since china s ban sources indicate that the united states is the largest importer of scrap into vietnam with around million pounds of plastics imported between january and may this reflects an increase of about million pounds from and million pounds from respectively in may port operating companies and customs offices experienced capacity constraints with containers being left at ports for more than to days in cat lai port alone there were about teus of long day stored goods teus of plastic and waste paper materials and a remaining teus of goods that were being stored for days or longer as a result many imported goods were left in queue at cai mep and tan cang hiep phuoc ports before they were moved to cat lai port thus creating a ripple congestion effect at other ports this led the authorities to impose a ban on waste imports on june the ports also stopped accepting plastic scrap shipments effective at all ports from june to october the temporary ban not only buys time for the ports to clean up the abandoned containers but also provides an opportunity for the authorities to formulate short and long term strategies to assess the ports storage capacity constraints and its plastic recycling industry it is evident that for its short term plan legislative actions against unlawful imports of scrap would be taken as the port authorities reportedly started cracking down on illegal shipments of paper plastic and metal scrap by investigating the owners of the containers and those responsible for the illegal imports furthermore the port authorities will take the ownership of inspecting permits of imported scrap containers before allowing vessels to unload sources indicate that authorities also found companies that were deliberately importing illegal waste under a false name with fake licenses and incorrect addresses to earn quick profits while they leave their trash at the terminals hence ports are now only allowing vessels to unload scrap containers if they have valid import permits and written date commitments to pick up the cargo moreover legal documents on the management of waste imports will be revised taking into account environmental protections and mechanisms to prevent control manage the trade and imports of scraps from other countries will be established despite these efforts as of early october there were still reportedly containers of scrap at cat lai port which includes containers that had been left for more than three months although the scrap import ban is temporary and is expected to last only for a few months it is likely that vietnam will gradually reduce the import of overseas scraps and simultaneously increase the reuse of recycled materials in its long term strategic approach solid waste ban had impacted local recycling industries as sources suggested that waste processing is an additional source of raw materials for the country s paper plastic and steel industries despite the environmental and port congestion concerns there is still a demand for overseas paper and plastic scraps for some domestic productions due to the inadequate plastic recycling system in the country sourcing of scrap locally is reportedly difficult as most plastic wastes are normally mixed with regular trash and are not separated properly ho chi minh city alone produces about tons of plastic waste daily of which only tons are recycled while there are pros and cons in the scrap policy efforts for local recyclers to switch to domestic waste will progress gradually in years to come as the industry needs time to adjust from handling import waste to domestic waste it is not only vietnam that needs to find a win win solution for both ports and the domestic recycling industry thailand and malaysia have also followed vietnam s footsteps in banning plastic waste due to an increase in such imports on july thailand was the second country after vietnam to ban the import of certain waste goods including plastic scrap electronic waste and hazardous waste at ports of laemchabang and songkhla however unlike vietnam the duration of the ban remains unclear for thailand in the same vein malaysia has cancelled the import licenses for of the country s plastic scrap processors and implemented new operating procedures and regulations for recyclable material import licenses sources indicated that authorities will conduct inspections to ensure that only processors with valid permits are allow to continue operations it is also important to note that indonesia had begun inspecting percent of scrap imports since early april following an increase in imports of scrap polystyrene from the united kingdom in the first three months of this year as most southeast asian nations take a tougher stance on waste import while they struggle with their own domestic waste problems waste shippers are left with fewer options to find alternative markets to substitute china it is no doubt that china s ban has disrupted the global supply chain which had about million tons of scrap plastic imported annually from the united states and europe although india is likely to be the next location where waste exporters were reportedly shipping to with volume up percent to teu there is no guarantee that this can remain a viable option in the long run perhaps china s import ban on scrap is a wake up call not only for southeast asian nations but also for countries with large volumes of scrap to find solutions in its domestic market particularly in the recycling sector

dispute around freight rates in brazil lead to congestion at ports the nationwide trucker strikes that swept through brazil during the last two weeks of may are continuing to have ripple effects throughout the country the most recent developments in this regard have been the negotiations between the government and the truckers over minimum freight haulage rates known as the tabela de frete or the minimum freight table the most notable result of this persistent dispute is its effect on sea ports over the past several weeks disputes between truckers and shippers have occurred at some of brazil s principal ports such as santos and paranagua this is evident in the backup of cargo at the aforementioned ports triggered by a dispute between shippers and truckers on what the agreed freight prices are shippers claim that the post strike rates are too high to make shipping affordable truckers on the other hand claim that the current rates were the best possible concession received during the course of the strike and any contestation of the rates will lead them back to strike a longer term issue lies with the government setting the definitive price schedule which it has done so far through a provisional measure this measure allows antt a national ground transportation entity to set the freight prices the brazilian supreme federal tribunal the highest court in the country has heard the arguments posed by both the government and truckers in court on june and is expected to announce its decision on august this however does not alleviate the immense pressure that the industry will be under pending the decision the continuing dispute has resulted in freight being stuck at ports with cargo vessels and containers backed up and unable to move until freight rate disputes are resolved no similar backlog has been reported in this context at any of the major international cargo airports in the country the use of air freight as an alternative to circumvent the backlog at the seaports may be considered agribusiness is the most immediately affected industry due to the perishability of the products involved until a decision is reached at the supreme federal tribunal in august customers with cargo at brazilian seaports are advised to keep abreast of new developments and where appropriate explore alternatives

at a central meeting point on campus at jnu to discuss their opposition to the citizenship amendment act caa and tuition fee hikes the attack lasted for approximately three hours and involved suspects physically assaulting students and faculty vandalizing residence halls and shouting provocative slogans at least people suffered injuries in the assault including four with serious injuries at this time there have been no reports of arrests made in connection with the attack in the immediate aftermath of the attack various left leaning organizations and students blamed akhil bharatiya vidyarthi in major nationwide demonstrations some of which have involved clashes between anti caa protesters pro caa protesters and police on december clashes between anti caa protesters and police in delhi that its tabangao refinery will be permanently refitted as a petroleum import terminal the move comes amid the global economic slowdown and lack of demand for oil caused by the covid pandemic the facility has been shut down since may according to both pilipinas shell and the philippines department of energy doe the conversion of the complex into an import terminal will not affect the oil supply in the philippines assessment the tabangao refinery located near the city of batangas some miles south of manila began operating in with a production capacity of barrels per day bpd with its transformation into an import terminal the philippines will be left with a single refinery petron s bpd facility near limay in bataan province petroleum demand in the philippines has fallen sharply during the covid outbreak with the doe reporting as much as a to percent decline in april demand currently remains down and is likely to have dropped again with the recent reimposition of heightened quarantine restrictions in metro manila and elsewhere in the country according to media reports pilipinas shell lost approximately us million in the first half of this year compared to a profitable period during the same time period last year according to the company its new import terminal will focus on supplying luzon and the northern visayas regions while its current north mindanao import facility will continue to deliver supplies to visayas and mindanao given the fact that oil refined at tabangao has already been put on the market and all oil coming from pilipinas shell since may has been imported as the company and the doe stated there is currently no reason to believe that oil supplies in the philippines will be negatively impacted by the change the global slowdown in the oil tanker hijacked by migrants reached malta as eu cuts patrol boat deployments from operation sophia on thursday five men were arrested after a tanker hijacked by migrants off the libyan coast reached the port of valletta under the command of maltese armed forces the elhiblu i palau flagged tanker had rescued migrants in the mediterranean sea tuesday evening and was heading to tripoli libya when it changed to a northward course about seven miles from the destination port the maltese military said thursday that the captain of the foot tanker had repeatedly said that he was not controlling the ship and that several migrants had threatened the captain and crew to make them head toward malta a maltese military patrol vessel blocked the tanker from entering territorial waters and a special operations unit subsequently boarded and regained control of the tanker the tanker was then piloted to valletta under navy escort where the five suspected hijacking leaders were arrested before the others disembarked there were no initial details of any possible injuries associated with the hijacking assessment the incident demonstrates migrants strong aversion to being taken to libya rather than a european destination after being rescued attempting to cross the mediterranean sea the hijacking occurred as the european union agreed in principle on a plan to extend its mediterranean migrant rescue patrols called operation sophia the eu announced wednesday that it plans to extend the operation by six months but would no longer deploy ships to patrol the sea instead relying on aircraft for monitoring the shift was based on strong resistance by the italian government which has previously refused to let ships with rescued migrants dock at its ports critics have argued that the limitation of the operation s rescue capacity imperils migrants still attempting to cross the sea a final decision on the operation extension terms is due by march although attempted crossings have reduced from the peak of the migrant crisis several years prior it remains to be seen whether commercial and other vessels may face greater pressure or obligation to rescue migrants as the potential nearest vessels and if the risk of additional incidents such as the tanker hijacking this week could increase resilience customers are advised to continue monitoring associated developments that may impact maritime operations in the mediterranean and the rates of migrants attempting crossings as summer approaches

arrests of protest leaders and banning of demonstrations likely to worsen hong kong situation on friday police arrested a number of prominent figures in the pro democracy movement including members of the demosisto party joshua wong chi fung and agnes chow ting and pro democracy lawmakers cheng chung tai au nok hin and jeremy tam man ho in total at least people were arrested their charges were related to protests that have taken place in recent months joshua wong and agnes chow have since been released on bail given evening curfews and have been prohibited from entering the admiralty area the day before police also prohibited the main rally called by the civil human rights front chrf on saturday citing the risk of violence due the history of other protests police said that they received credible intelligence that some protesters were planning to use petrol bombs tasers and drones against police the protest was scheduled to start at chater garden in central and end at beijing s hong kong liaison office in sai wan an appeal filed by the chrf was denied and as a result the march was officially canceled however a number of protesters have said that they intend to defy the ban and hold the protest march anyway police also banned a protest scheduled to take place on monday at salisbury garden in tsim sha tsui in kowloon that was meant to coincide with a two day strike called by the confederation of trade unions and other groups reports also emerged that earlier in the summer the hong kong government was prepared to make a key concession to the protesters in officially withdrawing the extradition bill that sparked the recent rounds of protests however beijing rejected the plan and instructed chief executive carrie lam to not withdraw the bill open a police inquiry or make any concessions to the protesters the plan was reportedly submitted to the central co ordination group for hong kong and macau affairs and was reviewed by chinese president xi jinping assessment the arrest of the prominent pro democracy figures the banning of protests and the refusal to make any concessions are likely to worsen the situation in hong kong in the immediate future these actions will likely further radicalize a portion of the more moderate protesters and some of the already more violent protesters now have even less reason to temper their actions if they feel that there are no other options the mass arrests were also likely timed to take place ahead of the five year anniversary of the release of the plan for limited democracy for hong kong on august dissatisfaction over the plan which required all candidates for chief executive to be approved by a pro beijing committee sparked the occupy central protests later that year despite the prohibitions on rallies it is likely that thousands of people will still be participating in demonstrations in the coming days and weeks even if overall numbers are down due to the threat of mass arrests as the protests will be unauthorized there is a much higher chance for clashes between protesters and police absent any central organizing group the protests are also likely to be more unpredictable in terms of location and march route and could spread to other areas of hong kong with little notice resilience customers are advised to closely monitor the situation and expect a strong police response to any unauthorized demonstrations all areas where protests are taking place should also be avoided due to the high risk of violence

shipping and warehousing services the attack has prompted the company to shut down many online services including online customer applications and package tracking and employees are reportedly unable to use company computers toll officials have stated that shipping is mostly unaffected although some customers may experience delays or other disruptions the company is prioritizing the shipment of covid related medical equipment toll s systems in new zealand where it is a major user of freight rail services were down for around hours beginning on monday morning but many were later restored including the toll global express online customer portal the company stated that it has been mainly using backup manual processes and will most likely continue to do so through the rest of the week assessment toll group a subsidiary of japan post that operates in some countries with approximately employees was hit by a ransomware attack in february that took five weeks for the company to completely recover from the company does not believe the current attack to be related to the earlier incident the type of ransomware being used in the present attack has been identified as nefilim which is often used by suspects who threaten to expose a company s data instead of simply erasing it if their payment demands are not met in toll s announcement of the attack the company stated that it had no reason to believe that any data had been extracted from its networks and said that the ransom demands would not be complied with the company is instead working to restore files using backup data clean affected servers and rebuild its core systems toll is working with the government s australian cyber security centre acsc on responding to the incident having recently experienced a similar situation with the ransomware incident in february the company may have better protocols in place for responding to the current crisis and it is possible that the recovery period this time may be swifter than the earlier incident nevertheless possible shipping delays and disruptions should be expected to continue at least through the end of the week and it is likely that some residual production cuts at shell and lyb as houston ship channel partially reopens as cleanup continues a seven mile stretch of the houston ship channel has partially reopened as of monday march following a three day closure due to contamination caused by a fire last week at an intercontinental terminals company itc facility in la porte tx the closure extended from tucker bayou which is near the itc facility to houston ship channel light the closure was initially enacted on friday due to multiple contaminants from the fire including gasoline suppressant foam and the chemical benzene being detected in the water as of this writing at least vessels were waiting to enter the channel and at least vessels were unable to leave the port of houston outbound traffic has reopened to vessels with less than a foot draft and only during daylight hours ships are moving through the opening spaced at approximately one hour intervals and all vessels are required to be inspected for chemical contaminates assessment cleanup efforts are ongoing but there remains no estimate for when the channel is expected to fully reopen to tanker traffic the u s coast guard is not expected to completely reopen the channel until it is confirmed that the benzene has dissipated and the oil runoff has been collected or dispersed several test vessels were initially sent through the affected area and were successful in not interfering with cleanup or being contaminated before the coast guard partially reopened the channel the houston ship channel closure has so far only affected tankers and there are no reports that any cruise or container ships have been impacted royal dutch shell and lyondellbasell industries lyb have both cut productions at their refineries located on the waterway due to the channel closure shell has reduced output by approximately barrels a day due to a shortage of crude oil a portion of the shell processing units remain in circulation so that normal production can resume quickly after the channel is fully reopened meanwhile lyb has cut production by approximately percent due to the inability to remove sulfur generated during fuel production and having limited storage on site as of yet there has not been a significant impact on the price of crude oil and officials do not anticipate the channel closure turning into a long term issue

drone equipment to the airport early on the morning of december local time two suspects who were arrested on the evening of december were released without charge on sunday assessment despite a detective s statement over the weekend that it was possible that there were never actually any drones near the airport sussex police said on monday that they could unequivocally state that there had been numerous sightings with the detective s doubt said to be a miscommunication based on the fact that no video evidence of drones had yet been acquired police were conducting house to house investigations near the airport over the weekend and were examining a damaged drone that was found near the airfield members of parliament have criticized the sussex police handling of the investigation including the misstatement over there being no drones and the apparent mistaken arrest of the two initial suspects and have suggested that london s metropolitan police might be better equipped to handle such a high profile investigation officials did not confirm what anti drone military equipment was dispatched to the airport but media sources reported that it was a drone dome system which is designed to interrupt communications between a drone and its operator defense officials consulted with the ceos of all uk airports on december with minister for security ben wallace saying that military counter measures can be deployed against drones at airports across the country if needed although it can be difficult to station certain types of equipment at civilian airports gatwick airport itself has spent us million million on unspecified additional anti drone technology since the start of the incident which it described as a deliberate act to disrupt the airport s operations the airport is also offering a us reward for information leading to suspects in the case with another being offered by the crimestoppers organization under uk law it is illegal to operate a drone within one kilometer miles of an airport and the maximum penalty for endangering an aircraft is five years imprisonment the case is being investigated under the aviation and maritime security act while there has been no indication that there is any ongoing imminent threat to gatwick or other airports from drones resilience customers are advised to expect associated travel disruptions in the event of further drone sightings

authorities warn that eln could be planning new offensive in northern and eastern departments on october th national liberation army eln insurgents killed two police officers in a grenade attack in a rural locality in the northern department of cesar two days later colombian authorities announced that they had obtained intelligence indicating that the rebel group was planning to launch a new offensive in the country s northern and eastern departments while few details have been publicly divulged the purported offensive has been likened to plan pistola a campaign of targeted police killings that a separate paramilitary group carried out last year police officers have been placed on high alert and elements of the colombian army have been deployed to rural police stations which are considered the most likely targets resilience advises travelers in colombia to take security precautions and practice strong situational awareness especially when in the vicinity of police stations any suspicious activity or items should be reported to local authorities recent developments on sunday october th two police officers were fatally ambushed on a road that links the municipalities of san alberto and la mata in the northern department of cesar the two officers had been tasked with conducting routine inspections of public transportation vehicles and were riding on a single motorcycle at the time of the attack unidentified assailants threw a hand grenade at the vehicle and then opened fire on the wounded officers with rifles before fleeing the scene both officers succumbed to their injuries authorities subsequently attributed the attack to the eln the following day president iv n duque held a press conference and stated that bogot would not resume peace talks with the eln should the group continue to carry out similar attacks on tuesday october th colombian authorities announced that they had obtained intelligence indicating that the eln was planning to launch a new offensive in the country s northern and eastern departments colonel iv n calixto commander of the magdalena medio police in the northwestern department of antioquia told reporters that the plot had been discovered through telephone intercepts authorities have likened the scheme to plan pistola an offensive carried out by the clan del golfo paramilitary group in mid which entailed a wave of attacks against police officers across the country although few additional details have been made public at this time colonel calixto stated that security measures were being bolstered throughout the region and that authorities were particularly concerned about the southern portion of bol var department which borders antioquia to the northeast the colombian army announced that it would provide additional support to police stations in rural areas which are considered to be the most likely targets background the most recent round of peace talks between bogot and the eln concluded on august st without any major progress since president duque took office on august th his administration has maintained a much more hard line stance than his predecessor duque has repeatedly stated that negotiations will only be resumed if the eln releases all of its captives ceases all criminal activity and declares a unilateral ceasefire while the insurgents have thus far failed to comply with these preconditions the eln made one concession in early september by releasing three police officers one soldier and two civilian contractors that the group had kidnapped the previous month nevertheless the eln continues to hold multiple captives on october th the rebels released a proof of life video of an engineer that they abducted from a rural locality in the northeastern department of arauca in march of this year historically the eln has engaged in kidnapping both to raise funds through ransom payments and to utilize abductees as bargaining chips as mentioned above the plan pistola offensive was an assassination campaign that was carried out last year by the clan del golfo a right wing paramilitary group and staunch adversary of the eln it entailed a wave of small scale attacks across ten departments which killed at least police officers and injured over more officers were targeted at police stations security checkpoints and while conducting routine patrols furthermore some officers were targeted while off duty during their commutes or at locations such as barbershops attacks were carried out with small arms grenades and improvised explosive devices ieds while most incidents occurred in small towns and rural localities some attacks transpired in larger cities such as cartagena and several plots were foiled in bogot and medell n assessment due to the scant details that have been made public so far it currently remains unclear to what extent the eln s purported offensive might resemble plan pistola as news of the eln s intentions has been made public and colombian security forces have already begun to take preventive measures it is possible that the guerillas could opt to delay modify or even abort the plan any renewed eln offensive could also potentially entail an uptick in attacks against fuel pipelines and other energy infrastructure the guerillas have historically favored this tactic as such attacks have proven to be a low risk and low cost means of both generating publicity and inflicting financial losses there are currently no signs to suggest that the diplomatic impasse between bogot and the eln will be overcome in the near future any large scale offensive by the eln would likely prompt a strong military response some local commentators have suggested that such a development might cause the duque administration to fully abandon the pursuit of a negotiated settlement with the rebels resilience advises customers with interests in colombia especially in bol var and other departments across the northern and eastern portions of the country to stay abreast of ongoing developments the eln has not historically engaged in indiscriminate attacks against civilian targets of opportunity nevertheless attacks directed against security forces have resulted in injuries and deaths of civilian bystanders and the group continues to occasionally target civilians in kidnappings due to the high level of risk posed by insurgent activity and violent crime resilience advises customers to avoid all travel to the departments of arauca norte de santander cauca choc and nari o travelers visiting other parts of the country are advised to take heightened security precautions especially in rural areas where police coverage may be severely deficient while the level of risk posed by the eln will likely be the greatest in rural areas the possibility of an attack in one of the nation s large cities cannot be ruled out entirely the eln demonstrated its continued ability to strike in urban areas when it detonated an ied in downtown bogot in february of travelers are advised to maintain a heightened sense of situational awareness when in the vicinity of police stations security checkpoints or military installations any atypical behavior or suspicious vehicles packages or objects should be promptly reported to local authorities

update australia s proposed legislation on agreements between states territories and foreign governments indicates increased likelihood of state contract cancellation the australian foreign relations state and territory arrangements act was introduced to parliament on september which would empower the federal government to cancel any written arrangement agreement contract understanding or undertaking between australian states and territories and foreign governments if these are assessed as being inconsistent with australian foreign policy prime minister scott morrison announced the legislation on august stating that the bill would ensure governments at the sub national level remain consistent with the national interest australian foreign minister and senator marise payne during the opening of senate business on may in canberra australia sam mooy getty imagestheforeign relations bill would apply to all foreign arrangements regardless of whether they are already in operation indicating that the law would be retroactive the proposed law does not cover commercial entities such as foreign state owned companies but is directed at government entities including national and subnational governments departments agencies and universities the bill includes the establishment of a public register where state territory entities would be required to disclose all existing foreign arrangements to the federal government ahead of a review by the foreign minister if the foreign minister considers that an arrangement is inconsistent with australia s foreign policy then he or she would have the power to terminate it arrangements likely to be terminated under the new law include a trade deal between the victorian and chinese governments that gives victoria access to funding under china s belt and road initiative sub national government entities would have to notify the federal government of any prospective foreign arrangements with core foreign arrangements which include arrangements with foreign countries their national governments and related departments and agencies requiring approval from the foreign minister in order to commence negotiations or enter the arrangement although the proposed legislation is not explicitly directed at a particular foreign government arrangements involving chinese government entities are most likely to be terminated concerns about chinese influence in australian politics and strategic assets has increased in recent years see australia january australian political interference laws likely to heighten scrutiny of foreign entities with australian subsidiaries within three months and in june the australian government proposed new rules tightening government scrutiny over foreign investments on national security grounds mitsubishi electric data breach highlights apt threat for manufacturers on january japanese electronics manufacturer mitsubishi electric disclosed the occurrence of a data breach that may have compromised information on government agencies and business partners while the firm confirms that sensitive information on defense electricity or other infrastructure operations have not been breached a total of workstations and servers were affected across all units of the company while personal data on over people including employees retirees and job seekers may have been endangered the hacking tools in question were discovered in a company lab based in japan on june unauthorized access occurred at the company s china affiliates before spreading to japan apt group believed to be responsible the suspected perpetrator of the hack is reportedly an advanced persistent threat apt group or a concerted and multifaceted professional hacking organization called tick also known as bronze butler or redbaldknight the apt group is believed to be based in china due to the use of chinese developer constructed tools documented links with the network crack program hacker ncph group as well as the start of unauthorized access in the company s china affiliates it is unlikely that the breach will have any operational impact and information security analysis suggests that the predominant focus of the group is the theft of intellectual property and sensitive communications a notable impediment to the resolution of this incident is the fact that the apt deleted access logs upon completion of the data theft thus complicating further investigation a task already made difficult by the group s frequent changing of communication ip addresses a signature of the group is the exploitation of a zero day flaw via spear phishing and strategic web compromises in yet to be identified software in northeast asia such as south korean defense firms and japanese heavy industry as well as miscellaneous targets in russia china and singapore the group s use of phishing disguised downloaders trojans and command and control servers make it a very conventional threat in terms of hacking playbook mitsubishi electric has already reinforced its information security and monitoring measures the company was the third largest contractor for major equipment at the japanese defense ministry in and provides cyber security services to public entities as well as private companies cyber security threat looms in japan while japan is advanced in technological development the country still lags behind others in addressing cyber attacks in fast retailing the parent company of popular japanese apparel brands such as uniqlo and gu japan suffered from credential stuffing attack that affected more than customers when the unknown hackers allegedly accessed its customers accounts from april to may customer information including name address phone number email addresses gender date of birth purchase history clothing measurements and credit card information were compromised when an authorized login by a third party was confirmed on may amidst this the japanese government has stepped up its measures against cyber security vulnerabilities prior to the upcoming summer olympic in tokyo the national institute of information and communications technology reportedly checked about million internet connected devices for potential cyber security vulnerabilities in however the recent case of mitsubishi electric highlights a wakeup call for other japanese manufacturing based firms to understand the growing threat of ransomware and spear phishing attacks and its implications on supply chains as the threat appears to have spread from consumer companies to manufacturers japan s national centre of incident readiness and strategy for cyber security detected billion cases of suspicious activity attributed to internet of things iot devices in a four fold increase from billion in multinational conglomerate like toshiba also observed an average of million attempted cyber attacks on a daily basis across its group of companies similarly mitsubishi heavy industries was hacked in which led to a virus proliferation across the company s locations including the kobe and nagasaki shipyards manufactured products such as the melsec q series ethernet module frequently employed alongside programmable logic controllers were found to have vulnerabilities when connected to the internet the controllers themselves were also found to have vulnerabilities cve as well as the company s fr configurator inverter engineering software staying resilient japan is yet to experience a large scale cyber attack causing disruption to services and operations while information technology firms are likely to be the targets of hackers a variety of japanese organizations in the fields of electric utility oil and natural gas transportation and construction are also vulnerable to such threats the risk of cyber attacks on manufacturers is amplified by the interconnectedness of businesses and it networks throughout northeast asia as a result the data breach by apt threat is unlikely to subside in the foreseeable future an important way to mitigate the impact of such incidents is to understand how cybercrime groups work and how to stymie their spread at each step of the process given the groups methods measures such as minimizing access privilege segmenting networks and adding signatures of the group to extant it security practices and outlining information security procedures can help protect one s systems furthermore the group is known to employ legitimate sites as hosts so examination of one s personal and environmental cyber risk can assist in the mitigation of future threats beyond it preparedness managing the security of a network as wide from japan to china and as connected across both the public and private sectors as that of mitsubishi electric necessitates visibility and communication in order to cascade warnings and mitigate threats throughout one s supply chain while data breaches are often quick and come to public knowledge well after the fact maintaining this level of visibility and communication from every indicator of risk from a vulnerability discovery to a phishing attempt can help reduce exposure across the supply chain

port workers in valparaiso threaten to resume day strike on november more than casual workers at chile s flagship port of valparaiso decided to walk off the job to demand a bonus payment more formal contracts and improved working conditions after a series of small demonstrations around dockworkers linked to terminal cerros de valparaiso tcval finally accepted an offer put forward by the port operator and returned to work on november the rest of the protesting workers however did not reach an agreement with terminal pac fico sur tps the second and most important concessionaire in valparaiso until december which shut down shipping for over days at one of chile s most important ports and a major commercial hub to the capital city santiago the first weeks of the strike were marked by small pickets outside the port facilities and union leaders negotiating with tps representatives in recent weeks however protests in valparaiso have turned increasingly violent and spread to other ports along the nation s pacific coast the conflict reached a tipping point on monday december when strikers set barricades throughout the city and police agents repressed demonstrators with water cannons and tear gas protesters also got into the dockers union headquarters resulting in detainees two injured and the destruction of much of the furniture in the building one day after the violent protests in valparaiso the striking dockworkers received support from their colleagues at the northern ports of iquique antofagasta caldera ventanas and san antonio the most important one in the country and close to valparaiso in the southern part of the country dockworkers at the ports of talcahuano san vicente and puerto montt also stopped their work in support of their colleagues in valparaiso the possibility of officially extending the strike to other ports in the country triggered alarms in sectors highly dependent on export activity such as agriculture food processing and chemicals which send products worth some usd billion to foreign markets each year impacts according to the chilean maritime port organization the strike has caused more than containers to be diverted to other ports with a total revenue loss of over usd million chile s fruit sector was particularly impacted by the strike in valparaiso which handles approximately of chile s fruit exports according to the federation of fruit producers of chile fruit shipments from the port of valparaiso fell as a result of the port strike going from tons between november and december in to only tons in meanwhile there was a large increase in shipments at the port of san antonio which had already displaced valparaiso in cargo handling and efficiency due to past port conflicts however not all was positive news for the port of san antonio which suffered from increased congestion due to more than additional trucks that arrived during the strike in a normal day according to san antonio s port authority there are about to trucks that are served in an hour however due to the massive arrival of operators from valparaiso it was necessary to attend to more than trucks in just one hour outlook on december the dockworkers union and the port operator tps reached a pre agreement which was later rejected by the dockworkers at a general assembly the workers argued that the compensations offered by tps are far below what they demand nonetheless on december workers at port of valparaiso ended their strike when union representatives accepted an offer from the operator tps following an agreement signed between the workers and the ministry of labor tps s offer includes a bonus of around pesos usd or eur a gift card of pesos usd or eur and a training course worth over pesos usd or eur on january however a group of port workers resumed demonstrations in valparaiso placing barricades near the dockworkers union headquarters protesters reportedly claim that port officials have not adhered to an initial payment agreement reached two weeks ago and that as many as dockworkers who participated in the december demonstrations have been denied access to the port facilities on the same day tps issued a public statement confirming that the port of valparaiso has continued to operate normally despite the most recent demonstrations lasting days the november december strike at the port of valparaiso was the second longest port strike in chile in the last years and one with important implications for the fruit industry in the country supply chain managers should continue to monitor the situation at the port of valparaiso because although operations have resumed further demonstrations are expected in the upcoming days moreover it will take weeks if not months to clear the congestion created as a result of the service disruption in valparaiso

clean_text: houthi missile attack on aramco facility in jeddah likely to spur calls for us terror designation on monday the yemen based houthi rebel movement claimed responsibility for a cruise missile attack that targeted a saudi aramco oil facility in the port city of jeddah hours earlier there were no initial reports of casualties from the attack on aramco s north jeddah bulk plant and a spokesman from the kingdom s energy ministry said that fuel supplies were not affected however a satellite photo suggested a fire was burning at the facility around am local time shortly after the attack reportedly occurred the united states consulate general in jeddah issued a security alert advising citizens to review immediate precautions to take in the event of an attack and stay alert in case of additional future attacks the message can be read here the november incident occurred hours after riyadh finished hosting the g leaders summit and as the us is considering designating the houthis as a foreign terrorist organization such an announcement which could be made as soon as next month would freeze all financial assets held by the houthis in us jurisdiction and also prohibit american citizens and organizations from providing material support or resources to the group assessment it stands to reason that monday s attack will increase the probability that washington will indeed tag the houthis as a terrorist group not only has the us maintained strong ties with saudi arabia under president donald trump and provided logistical and financial support to the saudi led coalition fighting the shi a rebels because the latter are seen as iranian proxies a designation would align with the white house s maximum pressure campaign on tehran and allies especially with the trump administration seemingly entering its final weeks in office however it is unclear if such a would have any meaningful impact on the houthis or the yemen conflict in general because the houthis are already regarded as isolated and given suggestions that the level of cooperation between the group and iran may be exaggerated blacklisting the yemeni rebels could have little more than symbolic value that said it could potentially exacerbate humanitarian conditions in yemen especially in houthi held sana a and the country s northern governorates by restricting the delivery of aid along with efforts to broker a peace deal by potentially subjecting aid agencies and other international organizations to sanctions more broadly monday s attack highlights the persistent threat of houthi fired projectiles in saudi arabia although most incidents occur along the kingdom s southern border and are purportedly intercepted by saudi air defenses the rebels have demonstrated a more sophisticated longer range arsenal giving them the ability to strike deep inside the country thus individuals in saudi arabia especially in the country s south should familiarize themselves with what to do in the event of a missile launch and review associated safety procedures

hong kong protests become more violent and less predictable requiring a higher level of caution on friday protests continued across hong kong with violent clashes taking place in the mong kok area of kowloon and the sheung shui area of the new territories in the evening protesters left the chinese university of hong kong cuhk which had been a flashpoint of clashes with police earlier in the week but some reportedly regrouped at hong kong polytechnic university polyu and others said they were planning to carry out different actions friday marked the fifth consecutive day where general strikes were called from the morning although the morning disruptions were much less severe when compared to earlier in the week individuals across hong kong also continued the daily action of walking out and occupying the streets during lunch although there were no reports of major clashes which took place earlier in the week as well the day before chinese president xi jinping issued another statement supporting hong kong chief executive carrie lam and called the protests a trampling of the rule of law and a blatant challenge to the one country two systems arrangement the u s china economic and security review commission which is a government body tasked with advising the u s congress also recommended that if beijing intervened militarily hong kong s special economic status should be suspended the recommendation is non binding and there were no reports that such a plan was in place assessment protests have entered a more violent and less predictable phase since monday with hong kong seeing daily general strikes that have resulted in widespread clashes and transportation disruptions protesters were generally satisfied with the disruptions seen in monday s action which led them to call for daily strikes through friday the lower impact of friday s general strike could be indicative of slowing momentum for the actions although it could also just be a temporary pause as protesters regroup the actions over the past week have also seen a notable shift in tactics that have made the demonstrations less predictable protesters have started to use blossom everywhere tactics which involve impromptu gatherings in the protesters own local neighborhoods the objective is to divide the attention of the police force and is also in response to the government shutting down the mtr system more quickly during protests which was used in the previous be water tactics that saw protesters spread from location to location by train flash mob tactics which involve the locations of demonstrations being announced just an hour or two before they start are also becoming more popular among protesters these developments in the protest movement make demonstrations more difficult to plan for in advance and necessitate a higher level of situational awareness being observed at all times some areas that have seen prolonged actions by protesters such as polyu and cuhk should be avoided the increased levels of violence over the past week which included a protester being shot a person being set on fire and a man dying after being hit by a brick have raised concerns that the chinese military could decide to intervene and restore order however this is an extreme step that would be an absolute last resort if it was clear that the government and police had lost control of the situation as it would likely have severe economic and political ramifications the hong kong government still has a number of other options available such as imposing additional restrictions under the emergency regulations ordinance ero which could include curfews greater powers for police or telecommunications restrictions that would likely be exercised before a military intervention took place it is still important to note that the situation remains very fluid and conditions could change quickly and all political and protest related developments should be closely monitored

india from china in the aftermath of the june border clash between indian and chinese troops according to indian media customs officers have received instructions to open all containers arriving from china and individually inspect every item inside normally only around percent of imported products arriving in india are physically inspected the ostensible reason given for the increased checks is that drugs have recently been intercepted in packages from china arriving in chennai but it is far more likely that the measures are intended as economic retaliation against china following the earlier clash indian officials have however denied that additional customs inspections have been ordered whether officially or otherwise the resulting shipping delays from the inspections are likely
